components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[-+()0-9 ]*$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be a
            syntactically valid address. It is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household

            Create-time flag. When true, allows creating this owner even though another owner
            already has the same last name and address (an intentionally shared household).

          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true

        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone

          properties:

              minimum: 0
              example: 1

              items:

              readOnly: true
            displayName:

              readOnly: true
            customerCode:

## What the change does

When a `POST /api/owners` request sets `sharesHousehold: true` and there's already an owner with the same last name and address, the new owner is allowed through (existing behavior) **and** now both the joiner and the existing household member(s) are stamped with the same stable `householdId`, which is returned on the owner resource.

## Changes

1. **`openapi.yml`** — Added a read-only `householdId` field to the `Owner` response schema, so it flows into the generated `OwnerDto` and is returned by `GET /api/owners/{id}` (via MapStruct's name-based mapping).

2. **`model/Owner.java`** — Added the `householdId` field (`@Column(name = "household_id")`) with getter/setter.

3. **DB schemas** (`db/{hsqldb,h2,mysql,postgres}/schema.sql`) — Added the `household_id` column to the `owners` table. The tests run on hsqldb with `ddl-auto=none`, so the schema.sql change is what actually creates the column; the others keep the dialects in sync.

4. **`rest/function/owner/AssignHousehold.java`** (new) — A pipeline step that, only when `sharesHousehold=true`, finds existing owners sharing the normalized last name + address, chooses a household id (reusing one already present, otherwise deriving a deterministic `H-<sha256 prefix>` from the normalized key), stamps it on the new owner, and back-fills + saves it onto existing members. The deterministic derivation guarantees every joiner computes the same id regardless of ordering or transaction visibility — which is what makes the identifier "stable" and "shared".

5. **`officefloor/rest/api/owners.POST.yml`** — Inserted the `household-assign` step (under `transaction` governance) between `build` and `customerCode`, so it runs on the built entity before it's saved.
